title: Trim Improvements | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive

The new update for trims in CLO 2025.0 allows you to attach trims to desired locations by tacking them to multiple points across various patterns. Check out other new features here: https://www.clo3d.com/en/clo/features

summary: ```markdown # Trim Improvements | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive ## Introduction Hey everyone, it's Phoebe, and I have a great update for you all with trims. So let's jump on in and have some fun while we learn! ## Overview of Trims To start, I'm going to do a little bit of a refresher on how you can add in trims and all of the updates because we did some cool updates in 2024.2 and 2025.0. Trims in general are good to have a refresher on, so let’s jump into it. ## Adding Trims First off, there are a few ways to add in trims. One way is by selecting the trim and using the glue bottle icon to attach it to your pants and then hitting simulate. Look at that! ### New Options for Trims In one of the last updates, we introduced an option that’s great for certain trims. You can actually pull it through a section. For example, let me select this trim and show you how it works. If I move this out and right-click while it's activated, I can hit simulate, and you'll see it just falls down now. ### Looping Through Fabrics What I can do is loop this through. Once it’s active, I hit simulate again, and now it will actively move within this piece of fabric, which is really cool, right? ## Important Note for Windows Users Something to know about this is important for all you Windows users. If you go to simulate GPU instead of CPU, this will not work. If I hit simulate and start to move this while on GPU, it won't function correctly. If you select the trim and right-click, it will be deactivated. So make sure to keep it on CPU when simulating and editing. ## Adjusting Trims As you can see, I was on GPU and it got a little messy. I can take the time to thread it through again using my tools, or I can rotate and move it back into position. This is one way to do it, and it’s totally legitimate. ## Introducing the Tack Tool Now, I want to introduce you to a new feature we added: the Tack Tool. When you click and select a trim, you’ll see a prompt next to the cursor saying to use the tack tool to attach multiple points. This feature is pretty straightforward. ### Using the Tack Tool You go to your tack tool or edit tack tool. This trim is already tacked, but I’ll delete it so you can see how it works. Select the tack tool, find the right placement, and note that the tacks will turn red instead of purple when correctly placed. ## Adjusting and Managing Tacks You can place as many tacks as you want. If you accidentally move them in the wrong direction, you can always edit and move them around. Remember to constantly adjust your perspective; it’s a great life lesson! ### Efficient Placement An efficient way to line them up is to place them directly on top of each other, making it much easier to manage. This is a brilliant idea, and I’m happy with how it turned out! ## Finalizing the Setup Once you’ve tacked everything, you can use the tack tool to make adjustments and fit the trims better. If you encounter any difficulties selecting, just move the trim out, go back to your tack tool, and make the necessary adjustments. ### Simulation After setting up your tacks, hit simulate, and everything will adhere together beautifully. ## Troubleshooting Tips If you run into issues, don’t panic. Sometimes it helps to deactivate certain components and let them figure themselves out. This can lead to better results. ### Additional Adjustments You can also go back and delete unnecessary items to clean up your workspace. If you need to attach something, you can select it and simulate again for a perfect finish. ## Closing Remarks Thank you so much for watching! If you have any questions, feel free to use the comment section down below. Don’t forget to like and subscribe, and check out all of the other videos within our Clo YouTube channel. I hope you enjoyed learning how to fix something unexpected today. We’ll see you next time! Keep having fun in Clo! ```
